description: Mole Negro, the queen of Oaxacan moles, is a culinary masterpiece known for its incredibly complex and rich flavor profile. This traditional black mole is a symphony of chiles, spices, nuts, seeds, and a touch of chocolate, creating a sauce that is both savory and subtly sweet. Preparing this mole is a labor of love, resulting in a deeply satisfying and unforgettable dining experience that truly embodies the heart of Mexican cuisine.

instructions.title: Prepare and Toast Chiles
instructions.text: Lightly toast the dried chiles (ancho, mulato, pasilla, chipotle) on a dry comal or skillet over medium heat for about 30 seconds per side, until fragrant but not burnt. Be careful not to over-toast. Immediately transfer them to a bowl of hot water and let them rehydrate for 20-30 minutes until soft. Drain and set aside.

instructions.title: Roast Aromatics and Spices
instructions.text: In the same comal or skillet, roast the tomatoes, tomatillos, onion, and unpeeled garlic cloves until softened and slightly charred. Separately, in a small dry pan, toast the almonds, peanuts, sesame seeds, and pumpkin seeds until lightly golden and fragrant. Also, lightly toast the cinnamon stick, cloves, peppercorns, and anise seeds.

instructions.title: Fry Plantain and Blend Ingredients
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of lard or oil in a pan and fry the sliced plantain until golden brown. In a blender, combine the rehydrated chiles, roasted vegetables, fried plantain, toasted nuts, seeds, and spices. Add about 1 cup of hot chicken broth and blend until a very smooth paste forms. You may need to do this in batches, adding more broth as needed to facilitate blending.

instructions.title: Simmer the Mole Base
instructions.text: Heat the remaining lard or oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Carefully pour the blended chile paste into the hot oil. It will splatter, so be cautious. Stir constantly for about 10-15 minutes, allowing the paste to cook and darken, intensifying its flavor. This step is crucial for developing the mole's depth.

instructions.title: Add Broth and Chocolate
instructions.text: Gradually add the remaining hot chicken broth to the simmering mole paste, stirring continuously to combine. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Add the Mexican chocolate tablet, stirring until it is completely melted and incorporated into the sauce. Continue to simmer the mole for at least 20-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken to your desired consistency.

instructions.title: Season and Serve
instructions.text: Season the mole with salt to taste. If the mole tastes a bit bitter, you can add a teaspoon of sugar to balance the flavors. Continue to simmer for a few more minutes. Serve the Mole Negro hot, traditionally over cooked chicken pieces, with a side of white rice and warm tortillas. Garnish with a sprinkle of sesame seeds if desired.

tips: For a truly authentic flavor, always toast your chiles and spices before rehydrating or grinding. This releases their essential oils and deepens their aroma.
If you want a silkier mole, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve or colander after blending to remove any remaining bits of chile skin or seeds.
Mole Negro improves with age. Make it a day ahead and gently reheat it on the stove, adding a little more broth if it has thickened too much. It freezes beautifully for up to 3 months.
